I think the issue of ad blocking and revenue is a colossal one, and not limited to the scope of gaming. The crux of the issue is that we've grown accustomed to malicious, annoying, or resource-wasteful advertising, so getting the average user to turn off their ad blocker for even one benign site takes some convincing.

Personally I don't mine a polite/respectful message, as long as it doesn't try to nag or guilt me. If it's a site I visit more than once, I'll likely disable my ad blocker.

I wish that Voat's native advertising model would gain support across the web. Native advertising solves a few problems:

  • it's less bandwidth intensive than loading third-party plugins
  • it's safer for the user because it doesn't load external and uncontrolled content
  • it's usually not actively blocked by ad blocking plugins because it's so similar to the site's other native content

The downside - and it's a big one - is it doesn't seem to pull as much revenue because advertisers aren't willing to trust the site-owner's own metrics to determine the number of unique impressions generated by the ad. One possible solution would be to create some kind of standard and low-impact plug-in that just counts impressions and doesn't negatively impact performance and security, but being a third-party plug-in it would likely be blocked by default in most ad blockers anyway.

I'm also interested in what Brave Browser is doing. Allowing users to voluntarily contribute X amount of dollars to their monthly browsing wallet, and at the end of the month split that money among the sites you've spent the most time on, as a compensation for blocking ads and a way to support the web while still blocking ads for performance and security reasons.

Any site that doesn't have an account set up to receive these funds has their funds put in escrow, and a notice sent to the site owner to collect when the funds value $100 or more.

It's an interesting puzzle with a handful of possible solutions, but none of them are perfect. My hope is that as web advertising gets worse and ad blocking becomes more attractive, the advertising industry will be more willing to settle for more user-friendly ad models and alternate funding models.
